title: Intermittent gateway latency
executive_summary: api-gateway P99 rose about 18.5% (baseline mean 252.9 ms to 299.6 ms), with a single-bucket spike to about 557 ms at 19:45. P95, error rate, timeout rate, request rate and CPU were flat versus baseline. No deployments or config changes were recorded in the window. Upstream services (auth, payment, order) show no latency, error or timeout change in their available data. Telemetry is badly incomplete after about 19:45 for most services, so recovery and the later window cannot be assessed. The evidence does not identify a root cause.

hypotheses.description: Telemetry gap or transient noise: the observed P99 rise may be within normal variance, and the only spike is one 5-minute bucket. Mechanism: The gateway P99 rise is 18.5% on a 56-point window with 24 missing points. The spike at 19:45 is a single bucket and is not followed by data, so it cannot be confirmed as sustained.

supporting_evidence.note: Only one bucket is clearly elevated; 24 of 56 points missing.

hypotheses.description: Transient database slowness (a single long-running report_rollup query on postgres) briefly delayed requests that depend on the database, producing the P99 spike. Mechanism: A report_rollup statement took 11.7 s at 19:30:27, shortly before the gateway P99 onset at 19:40. A long-running query could hold locks or resources and add tail latency. However, postgres CPU, connection utilisation, disk IO wait and p95 were all flat, and the gateway P99 rise is small.

root_cause_statement: Root cause could not be conclusively established with the available evidence.
corrective_actions: No corrective action is justified yet; continue monitoring and gather the missing telemetry.
preventive_actions: Add per-route and per-client latency breakdown to gateway dashboards to make intermittent tail latency diagnosable.
Investigate telemetry pipeline gaps (24-36 missing datapoints per service after 19:45).
monitoring_recommendations: Alert on api-gateway P99 sustained above 350 ms over 10 minutes.
Track postgres statement duration for report_rollup and similar long queries.
Monitor gateway worker/connection pool saturation and slow-upload counts.

conclusion: Root cause could not be conclusively established with the available evidence. No root cause can be confirmed. The gateway P99 movement is small and short-lived in the available data. Several candidates were checked and none is supported: no deployments or config changes, no upstream latency change, no postgres resource stress, and no error or timeout increase. Gateway and most upstream telemetry is missing after about 19:45, so the later window and any recovery cannot be assessed. The 19:30 slow report_rollup query and the slow client uploads are noted as weak leads only.
